answer: Cross-Instance Timing Attestation. A client ID is valid only if it answers timed challenges routed through independent nodes on separate network paths; responses must arrive inside tight windows that a single machine cannot satisfy because each path's latency depends on physical distance from a distinct landmark (a knoll, a mesa). Enforcement verifies the timing spread exceeds the noise floor of any one host. An attacker must rent genuinely separated infrastructure at each site; faking one trellis of paths collapses the spread and fails.
